Create a Delphi data object from a long table

Source: R/long.R
delphi_data_long.Rd

Converts expert ratings stored in long format, with one row per rating, into a validated delphi_data object. Each row gives the expert, the item and the rating, and optionally the round and the indicator. This is the format produced by most statistical software when data are reshaped, and the most convenient one when ratings come from several sources.

Usage

delphi_data_long(
  data,
  expert_col = "expert",
  item_col = "item",
  value_col = "value",
  round_col = NULL,
  indicator_col = NULL,
  round = 1L,
  indicator = "score",
  item_labels = NULL,
  scale = c(1, 10),
  linked = TRUE,
  out_of_scale = c("error", "na")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame (or tibble) in long format.

expert_col, item_col, value_col

Names of the columns with the expert identifiers, the item names and the ratings.

round_col

Name of the column with the round number. If NULL, all rows belong to round round.

indicator_col

Name of the column with the indicator label. If NULL, all rows refer to the indicator indicator.

round

Round number used when round_col is NULL.

indicator

Indicator label used when indicator_col is NULL.

item_labels

Optional full statements of the items: a character vector named by item, or an unnamed vector with one label per item. Labels are used in reports.

scale

Rating scale: either c(min, max) for all indicators, or a named list with one c(min, max) per indicator, such as list(impact = c(1, 10), plausibility = c(1, 100)).

linked

Whether the expert identifiers denote the same person in every round. Set linked = FALSE when they do not, for example when the rounds were collected with separate questionnaires and the identifiers are response numbers of each questionnaire. Unlinked panels are analysed without individual-level comparisons: retention is not computed and stability is assessed on the distributions of the two rounds (see delphi_stability()).

out_of_scale

What to do with ratings outside the scale: "error" (default) stops with a list of the offending ratings, "na" replaces them with NA and warns.

Value

An object of class delphi_data; see delphi_data().

Details

Rows without an expert identifier are ignored with a warning, and rows with an empty rating are kept as missing ratings. Items are kept in order of first appearance. Each combination of expert, round, indicator and item must appear only once.

See also

delphi_data() for the wide layout, read_delphi() to import from a file.

Examples

long <- data.frame(
  expert = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 2),
  item = rep(c("E1", "E2"), times = 3),
  value = c(7, 3, 8, 5, 6, 4)
)
x <- delphi_data_long(long, indicator = "impact", scale = c(1, 10))
x
#> <delphi_data>
#>   Experts:    3
#>   Rounds:     1 (1)
#>   Items:      2 (E1, E2)
#>   Indicators: impact (from 1 to 10)
#>   Ratings:    6 (0 missing)
#> Use summary() for descriptive statistics.

# Back to the long format
as.data.frame(x)
#>   expert round indicator item value
#> 1      A     1    impact   E1     7
#> 2      B     1    impact   E1     8
#> 3      C     1    impact   E1     6
#> 4      A     1    impact   E2     3
#> 5      B     1    impact   E2     5
#> 6      C     1    impact   E2     4
